title: Reprint · the postcard run, i
logline: The 2001 postcard strip, re-inked. The 2010 hand redraws her 2001 handwriting and shakes on it — the one place in the reprints where the re-ink is worse than the original, and the book keeps it for that.

margin.note: A second, smaller date under the crab: 2001.

panels.composition: The 2001 bedroom, drawn in 2010: WOOD, twenty, with a postcard. BARNABY, one. The corkboard.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a young man on a bed holding a postcard with a small dog beside him and a corkboard behind, drawn in a clean steady line
image.notes: Reprint of dw_2001-05-18. The book prints the original beside it.

panels.composition: The postcard's writing side: her hand, redrawn. The 2010 line wavers on the letters. The only wobble in nine months of re-inks.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, close-up of a postcard's handwritten message where the ink line visibly wavers on the letters, no words
image.notes: The re-ink is worse here than the 2001 original. The book keeps it for that.

panels.composition: Wood pinning it. The corkboard: the 2001 board, drawn from memory in 2010, with things on it that weren't there yet. A small anachronism the strip lets stand.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a young man pinning a postcard to a corkboard that holds a few items from later years, no words
image.notes: Reserved which items are anachronistic; suggest the 2003 rough's pinholes.

panels.composition: The dog, one, on the bed, drawn with the knowledge of the dog at eleven. The strip can't help it.

characters.pose: one, drawn by someone who knows him at eleven

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a small young dog on a bed drawn with the tenderness of someone who has known it for a decade, no words

notes: Reprint pair, the postcard. The hand wavers on her writing.
